name: 00-intro
title: Nativeproof
subtitle: A real session on nativeproof.vercel.app with live Qloo data and live models
narration: This is Nativeproof, a research workspace that tests how a campaign may land in another culture before money is spent on it. Everything in this video is one real session on the deployed app, recorded on October twenty-ninth: live Qloo cultural data, live language models, and synthetic participants. The participants are generated by AI. They are not real people, and the app labels them that way everywhere.

name: 01-sign-in
title: Sign in
subtitle: Judging account; Google sign-in and an anonymous demo are also available
narration: We sign in with the judging account. Google sign-in is on the same page, and Try the demo starts an anonymous session on clearly labeled fixture data. This session uses live mode only.

name: 02-project
title: Project, brand kit and campaign
subtitle: Every edit creates a new content version
narration: We create a live project for a fictional brand, Trailhead Coffee, launching canned cold brew for weekend hikers in Japan. The brand kit records the voice, terms that must stay verbatim, and terms that are not allowed. Then we add the campaign copy and the cultural references to investigate. Every edit creates a new content version, so each later result names exactly which copy it tested.

name: 03-atlas
title: Atlas: Qloo evidence
subtitle: Ambiguous matches are confirmed by a person, never guessed
narration: Atlas resolves the campaign's concepts against Qloo. In this live run, all five terms came back ambiguous. Qloo holds several tags named Hiking, for example as a hobby, an activity and a lifestyle. Nativeproof does not guess. It lists the candidates, and we confirm one with Use this. Each choice re-runs discovery, and each run took between thirty and sixty-six seconds. With all five confirmed, ten signals resolved. The market brief separates source data from model interpretation, and its risks state plainly that affinity data does not prove demand.

name: 04-rehearsal
title: Quick rehearsal
subtitle: A study with research questions, grounded in discovery evidence
narration: A population study builds on a study, so we create one with two research questions and run the quick rehearsal. It generated twelve synthetic reactions grounded in ten discovery evidence records, in fifty-six seconds. It raised something we had not considered: several reactions were unsure how hikers would carry and dispose of the can.

name: 05-population-start
title: Population study: 100 participants
subtitle: Background run with checkpoints, cancel and resume
narration: Now the main study. We build a new synthetic population of one hundred participants for Japan at standard interview depth, and we upload the ad creative, so participants react to what a vision model actually observes in the image. The study runs in the background and saves checkpoints. It can be cancelled or resumed, and a server restart marks it resumable instead of losing the work.

name: 06-population-results
title: Population results
subtitle: Deterministic tallies of stored interviews
narration: The study finished in two minutes and twenty seconds, and all one hundred interviews completed. Seventy-one percent were positive, twelve mixed and seventeen neutral, with none negative or confused. The participants come from four groups built from the Qloo evidence, twenty-five in each. Every number is a tally of stored interviews, not a model's estimate. The reaction graph links campaign elements, groups, reactions and themes. The landscape maps the groups to their Qloo interests. Every interview is labeled as AI-generated, and the recommendations name their own gaps, such as the absence of negative voices.

name: 07-social-simulation
title: Multi-round social simulation
subtitle: Stance changes with reasons and the posts that caused them
narration: Next, a three round social simulation. In each round, twenty percent of the participants read a feed of five peer posts, then post, comment, share or ignore. It completed in seventy seconds, with nine, four and eight stance changes across the rounds. Each post records the stance before and after, the participant's stated reason, and the exact posts it reacted to, so every claimed influence can be traced back to its source.

name: 22-diffusion
title: Social diffusion graph
subtitle: Audience groups and posts, round by round
narration: The diffusion view draws the simulation as a graph of audience groups and their posts, round by round, and the feed browser filters every post by round and by group. The view is labeled as illustrative. It is not a forecast of real reach.

name: 08-follow-ups
title: Participant memory and follow-ups
subtitle: Answers cite stored memories and become memories
narration: Participants keep memory. This participant's current stance comes from round one, and its memories are its interview and its own post. We ask a follow-up about carrying the empty can back down. The answer cites one stored memory and is saved as a new memory. We can also question a whole group. A seeded sample of five answered, and the tally covers only that sample.

name: 10-risk-radar
title: Risk Radar with vision
subtitle: Observations kept apart from interpretations
narration: Risk Radar scans the copy and the image together. A vision model, MiniCPM-V, analyzed the uploaded creative. In twenty-seven seconds the scan found five potential issues, one moderate and four low. The moderate one is the line, crack one open at the summit, which the model reads as a possible clash with etiquette at sacred peaks in Japan. That reading is labeled as model interpretation. Applying the suggested change creates a new adaptation. The campaign itself is never edited in place.

name: 11-voice
title: Voice adaptations
subtitle: Every change shows what it replaces and why
narration: Voice writes market adaptations, grounded in the discovery evidence and the rehearsal findings. It produced two variants in about fifteen seconds. Each change shows what it replaces, why, and whether evidence supports it, and deterministic checks confirm that protected terms were kept and prohibited terms avoided.

name: 12-loop-evaluation
title: Loop evaluation
subtitle: Deterministic decision rules, no invented winner
narration: Loop scores the original and three candidates under one scoring version. The best candidate scored ninety point five against eighty-five point eight. Because the margin is under five points, the decision rule recommends validating with real people instead of declaring a winner.

name: 13-version-comparison
title: Versions on identical participants
subtitle: Same 100-person population, version 2 against version 3
narration: Loop can also compare versions on identical participants. We saved the risk fix as version three and interviewed the same one hundred participants again. Reusing the population skipped all Qloo and construction work. The result is honest: positive reactions fell from seventy-one to sixty-six percent. The fix may remove a cultural risk but cost emotional pull, and the app states that no statistical significance is claimed.

name: 21-cancel-resume
title: Cancel and recovery
subtitle: A run stops at a checkpoint and keeps its finished work
narration: Long runs can be cancelled. We start another study on the same population and cancel it after the first batch. It stops at the next checkpoint and keeps what was finished: forty of one hundred interviews, saved and readable. A cancelled run is final. Resume is for runs that failed or were interrupted, for example by a server restart. When we restarted the server during the next run, Render kept the old instance running until the new one was healthy, so that run simply completed. Recovery after a hard stop is covered by the automated tests.

name: 18-arena
title: Campaign Arena
subtitle: Concepts side by side for one audience and one set of criteria
narration: Campaign Arena puts concepts side by side for the same synthetic audience and the same criteria. In eighty seconds, variant B led with ninety-three point eight out of a hundred, and the original was marked as within five points of the leader.

name: 16-cultural-dna
title: Cultural DNA
subtitle: A versioned profile where every item cites evidence
narration: Cultural DNA turns the discovery evidence into a versioned cultural profile, in under thirty seconds. Every item cites its Qloo source, and items without support are labeled as hypotheses.

name: 17-market-expansion
title: Market Expansion
subtitle: A real limitation, reported instead of filled in
narration: Market Expansion runs the same discovery across several markets. Here it shows a real limitation. Its terms came back ambiguous in both Japan and South Korea, and this screen does not yet have a confirmation step, so both markets are reported as unavailable instead of being ranked on missing data.

name: 19-brand-trend
title: Brand Memory and Trend Watch
subtitle: Rules every workflow reads; snapshots compared deterministically
narration: Brand Memory stores the rules every workflow reads. Trend Watch compares two saved discovery snapshots without calling a model. It shows which signals appeared and disappeared, and it warns that two snapshots are not a trend line, and that a difference can come from matching changes rather than culture.

name: 14-evidence-graph
title: Evidence Graph
subtitle: Only stored links are drawn
narration: The Evidence Graph draws only links the system stored: one hundred and fifty-three nodes and one hundred and seventy edges from this session. Selecting a node shows its provenance. This one is a cached Qloo source signal, produced by a discovery run, with its limitations attached.

name: 15-proof-report
title: Proof report
subtitle: Assembled from stored results, with reproducibility details
narration: Finally, Proof assembles a report in thirteen seconds without calling a model. It carries the verdict, the evidence register, the limitations, and a reproducibility section with model identifiers, prompt versions, and each stage's provider and latency. It exports as Markdown, JSON or PDF.

name: 20-home
title: Home dashboard
subtitle: Counts of stored records across the account
narration: Back on Home, the dashboard counts what this session produced: one project, one market researched, one hundred and nine evidence records, and the recent completed runs. Each number is a count of stored records, not an estimate.

name: 99-outro
title: Validate with real people
subtitle: github.com/vishavmehra/NativeProof
narration: Nativeproof helps teams find cultural risks and opportunities before launch, and it says clearly when the evidence is not enough. Synthetic participants are a tool for forming hypotheses. Decisions still need validation with real people. The code, diagrams and setup guide are on GitHub.
